title: Power Automate: schedule desktop flows directly with scheduled triggers
summary: The roadmap facts, preview qualifications, schedule-management instructions, licensing background and data-policy controls are supported. Independent searches found no documented tenant-wide or environment-wide availability switch, or separate scheduled-trigger price.

claims.claim: This Power Automate feature lets makers schedule desktop flows directly.
claims.quote: Power Automate: Schedule desktop flows directly with Scheduled Triggers

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Scheduled triggers remove the need for an intermediary scheduled cloud flow.
claims.quote: eliminating the need to create and manage intermediary scheduled cloud flows

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Makers run desktop flows on a recurring schedule from the Power Automate automation center.
claims.quote: Scheduled triggers enable makers to run desktop flows on a recurring schedule directly from the Power Automate automation center

claims.claim: The roadmap describes daily, weekly, monthly, hourly and custom recurrence patterns.
claims.quote: Users can configure daily, weekly, monthly, hourly, or custom recurrence patterns

claims.claim: Makers can select an execution machine or machine group.
claims.quote: select the execution machine or machine group

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a centralized view of upcoming scheduled runs.
claims.quote: monitor upcoming scheduled runs from a centralized experience

claims.claim: The roadmap covers both attended and unattended desktop flows.
claims.quote: a more intuitive scheduling experience for attended and unattended desktop flows

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview as release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap cloud list is Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence or billing meter.
claims.quote: Scheduled triggers enable makers to run desktop flows on a recurring schedule directly from the Power Automate automation center, eliminating the need to create and manage intermediary scheduled cloud flows.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not identify a run's identity or connection, or describe data access beyond the desktop flow.
claims.quote: Users can configure daily, weekly, monthly, hourly, or custom recurrence patterns, select the execution machine or machine group, and monitor upcoming scheduled runs from a centralized experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes Scheduled triggers as preview, despite the roadmap's Launched status.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The preview is gradually rolling out across regions and may not yet be available in a reader's region.
claims.quote: This feature is being gradually rolled out across regions and might not be available yet in your region.

claims.claim: In Power Automate, select the target environment, then Automation center > Manage > Scheduled triggers (Preview) > New.
claims.quote: select the environment where you want to manage scheduled triggers. In the left navigation pane, select Automation center. Under Manage, select Scheduled triggers (Preview).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Upcoming tab displays projected scheduled-trigger executions.
claims.quote: Select the Upcoming tab to view projected scheduled-trigger executions.

claims.claim: The Overview tab lists scheduled triggers available to the user.
claims.quote: The Overview tab lists the scheduled triggers available to you.

claims.claim: Turning on Enable activates a newly created schedule.
claims.quote: To activate the trigger immediately after you create it, turn on Enable.

claims.claim: Leaving Enable off saves the trigger as disabled.
claims.quote: Turn on the scheduled trigger so that it can create scheduled runs. Leave it off to save the trigger as disabled.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: An individual trigger can be disabled through Automation center > Manage > Scheduled triggers (Preview) > Overview > its More commands menu > Disable.
claims.quote: On the Overview tab, open the More commands menu for the scheduled trigger that you want to manage. Select Disable for an enabled trigger.

claims.claim: Disabling a scheduled trigger stops future scheduled runs without deleting its configuration.
claims.quote: Disabling a scheduled trigger stops future scheduled runs without deleting its configuration.

claims.claim: Cloud flows can trigger desktop flows through events, schedules and buttons.
claims.quote: Power Automate enables you to trigger desktop flows from cloud flows using events, schedules, and buttons.

claims.claim: The cloud-flow trigger route requires a registered machine or machine group.
claims.quote: A registered machine or machine group that will run the triggered desktop flows.

claims.claim: The cloud-flow trigger route requires a work or school account.
claims.quote: A work or school account.

claims.claim: The cloud-flow trigger route requires a configured desktop flow connection.
claims.quote: A configured desktop flow connection.

claims.claim: Automation center is a centralized monitoring and troubleshooting hub.
claims.quote: the automation center serves as a centralized hub to monitor and manage automation activity within your environment

claims.claim: Automation center's Runs page displays cloud and desktop flow execution data.
claims.quote: Runs: View and analyze cloud and desktop flow execution data with filtering options for overview, run history, and current desktop flow runs.

claims.claim: Automation center's Machines page monitors machine and machine group status.
claims.quote: Machines: Manage and monitor machine and machine group status and connectivity.

claims.claim: A scheduled cloud flow runs under its owner's licence.
claims.quote: If the flow is a scheduled or automated flow, after the owner changes, the flow runs under the license of the new owner and uses their Power Platform request limits.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: For cloud-triggered attended desktop flows, the appropriate licence is required for the creator of the connection.
claims.quote: To run the triggered desktop flows, you need to have the appropriate license (for attended runs) or an unattended add-on (for unattended runs). The user who needs to have the appropriate license is the creator of the connection.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cloud-trigger page specifies an unattended add-on for unattended runs.
claims.quote: To run the triggered desktop flows, you need to have the appropriate license (for attended runs) or an unattended add-on (for unattended runs).

claims.claim: Learn does not specify which cloud-route-specific owner licensing, connection and data-policy checks carry over to direct scheduled triggers.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" desktop flow connection credentials identity licensing connection creator; "scheduled triggers" "desktop" "data policies" connector DLP evaluation. Read Scheduled triggers, Trigger desktop flows, licensing, meters and DLP pages; no inherited-check mapping found.

claims.claim: Data policies classify desktop flow modules as Business, Non-business or Blocked.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: Noncompliant desktop flows are suspended when evaluated against desktop flow DLP policies.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: A difference between DLP evaluation of scheduled-trigger runs and cloud-triggered runs is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" "desktop" "data policies" connector DLP evaluation. Read Scheduled triggers and Data loss prevention (DLP) policy creation; neither describes a scheduled-trigger-specific difference in desktop-flow DLP evaluation.

claims.claim: The unattended-run page says unattended desktop flows require an available machine with all users signed out.
claims.quote: Unattended desktop flows require an available machine with all users signed out.

claims.claim: The unattended-run page says locked Windows user sessions prevent unattended runs.
claims.quote: Locked Windows user sessions will prevent unattended desktop flows from running.

claims.claim: The reuse Windows session option locks a session after a run and allows Power Automate to reuse it.
claims.quote: The reuse Windows session functionality allows desktop flows to run on an existing session. After a desktop flow run, the session gets locked, and Power Automate can reuse it for another run.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop flows execute without human supervision.
claims.quote: Unattended run mode refers to a desktop flow execution without human supervision

claims.claim: The desktop-flow orchestration page documents a timeout if a requested desktop flow does not run within 12 hours.
claims.quote: A time-out occurs when desktop flows don't run within 12 hours after being requested.

claims.claim: The orchestration page says its rules apply to desktop flow runs scheduled by any user on the same device.
claims.quote: The presented orchestration rules apply to desktop flow runs scheduled by any user on the same device.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant-wide or environment-wide availability switch for scheduled triggers is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" availability tenant settings Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell disable environment. Read Scheduled triggers, Tenant settings, Flow Trigger reference and pac admin search excerpts; found individual-trigger controls, not an availability switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: makers choose to create and enable schedules where it is available.
claims.quote: On Scheduled triggers, select New. To activate the trigger immediately after you create it, turn on Enable. Leave it off to save the trigger as disabled.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, reflecting desktop-flow user licensing, unattended capacity licensing and pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Power Automate supports both user and capacity licensing. For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licensing requirement specific to scheduled triggers is published, beyond desktop-flow run-mode requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" "desktop" "license" pricing meter. Read Scheduled triggers prerequisites, Types of Power Automate licenses and Pay-as-you-go meters; found run-mode licensing and capacity requirements, not a separate scheduled-trigger licence.

claims.claim: The licence overview identifies Process licences or pay-as-you-go for running desktop flows unattended.
claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: A Process licence allocated to a machine becomes an unattended bot that runs one desktop flow at a time.
claims.quote: When allocated to a machine, a Process license becomes an unattended bot that can run one desktop flow at a time.

claims.claim: The Power Automate pay-as-you-go meters are marked preview.
claims.quote: Power Automate meters (preview)

claims.claim: Unattended desktop-flow runs in a pay-as-you-go environment cost $3.00 per run.
claims.quote: Unattended runs are charged at $3.00 per run regardless of any capacity assigned to the environment.

claims.claim: Attended pay-as-you-go desktop-flow runs are not charged when the running user's licence includes attended RPA.
claims.quote: Attended runs follow the entitlements of the user running the flow. A user whose license includes attended RPA isn't charged

claims.claim: Attended pay-as-you-go desktop-flow runs cost $0.60 per run when the running user's licence lacks attended RPA.
claims.quote: a user whose license doesn't include it is charged $0.60 per run.

claims.claim: No rate or billing exception specific to scheduled triggers is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" "desktop" "license" pricing meter. Read Scheduled triggers, Types of Power Automate licenses and Pay-as-you-go meters; found general desktop-flow rates and entitlements, not a scheduled-trigger-specific rate or exception.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Variable cost is supported by per-run pay-as-you-go metering, so additional scheduled runs can increase charges.
claims.quote: The Power Automate meters enable users to build and/or run premium Power Automate flows and to pay for their usage based on the number of times these flows run instead of purchasing standalone Power Automate licenses.

claims.claim: The schedule owner and users assigned the Power Automate Operator role can manage schedules where Scheduled triggers is available.
claims.quote: In environments where Scheduled triggers is available, users assigned the Power Automate Operator role can manage desktop-flow schedules, in addition to the schedule owner.

claims.claim: Operator schedule-management permissions apply across the assigned environment, not only to the operator's own records.
claims.quote: These permissions apply to the entire environment where the role is assigned, not just to records owned by the operator.

claims.claim: The Operator role itself does not grant permission to create or modify the underlying desktop flow definition.
claims.quote: The Operator role itself doesn't grant permission to create or modify the underlying desktop flow definition.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require a work or school account with access to the target environment.
claims.quote: A work or school account that can access the target Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: Creating a scheduled trigger requires a published desktop flow that the user owns or co-owns.
claims.quote: A published desktop flow that you own or co-own.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require a machine or machine group registered in the same environment.
claims.quote: A machine or machine group registered in the same environment.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require a connection reference for the target machine or machine group.
claims.quote: A connection reference for the target machine or machine group. You can create the connection reference while creating the scheduled trigger.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require licensing and capacity for the selected attended or unattended run mode.
claims.quote: The licensing and capacity required for the selected attended or unattended run mode.

claims.claim: The Flow Trigger table reference documents PATCH /flowtriggers(flowtriggerid).
claims.quote: Update Event: True | PATCH /flowtriggers(flowtriggerid)

claims.claim: The Flow Trigger reference documents updating statecode and statuscode through that PATCH operation.
claims.quote: SetState Event: True | PATCH /flowtriggers(flowtriggerid) Update the statecode and statuscode properties.

claims.claim: The Operator role includes permissions for the Flow trigger and Flow trigger instance tables.
claims.quote: The Operator role includes organization-level permissions for the Flow trigger and Flow trigger instance tables.

claims.claim: A data policy can govern both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.
claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The desktop flow connector can be governed in data policies like any other connector.
claims.quote: The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether direct scheduled triggers are evaluated through the desktop flow connector.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" "desktop" "data policies" connector DLP evaluation. Read Scheduled triggers and Data loss prevention (DLP) policy creation; the connector is governable, but neither page identifies it as the evaluation route for direct scheduled triggers.

claims.claim: The documented tenant-level data-policy steps require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: The environment-level data-policy steps require Environment Admin permissions outside the Dataverse qualification.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: For environments with a Dataverse database, the environment-level data-policy steps require System Administrator instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business reaches connector classification.
claims.quote: From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy. Select the Prebuilt connectors step in the Edit Policy process. Select one or more pre-built connectors. ... select Move to Business from the top menu bar.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <classification> classifies connectors or desktop flow modules in a DLP policy.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> [[-ApiVersion] <String>] [<CommonParameters>]

claims.claim: To show desktop flow action groups in the DLP policy UI, enable Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies.
claims.quote: By default, desktop flow action groups don't appear when you're creating a DLP policy. You need to turn on the Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies setting in your tenant settings.

claims.claim: Desktop flow modules must be explicitly classified for DLP evaluation to enforce their classification.
claims.quote: only desktop flow modules that are explicitly classified in a policy group (Business, Non-business, or Blocked) are enforced during DLP evaluation

claims.claim: Classification accepts General, Confidential and Blocked for Non-business, Business and Blocked respectively.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: The roadmap describes changes for desktop-flow makers and names no change for other users.
claims.quote: Scheduled triggers enable makers to run desktop flows on a recurring schedule directly from the Power Automate automation center
